Class SpringBidiMappingService

java.lang.Object
org.openehealth.ipf.commons.map.BidiMappingService
org.openehealth.ipf.commons.spring.map.SpringBidiMappingService
All Implemented Interfaces:
MappingService, MappingResourceTarget, Aware, BeanFactoryAware, SmartInitializingSingleton
@Deprecated(since="6.0", forRemoval=true) public class SpringBidiMappingService extends BidiMappingService implements MappingResourceTarget, BeanFactoryAware, SmartInitializingSingleton
Deprecated, for removal: This API element is subject to removal in a future version.
as of 6.0, use SpringMappings and the typed Mappings API. This class remains as an adapter for applications still holding a MappingService, and is scheduled for removal in IPF 7.0.
BidiMappingService implementation that can be configured with Spring resources.

A resource is dispatched to a loader by its file extension, so the mapping files an application registers may be in any format whose module is on the classpath - .mapping.xml, .mapping.yaml, .conceptmap.r4.json or the legacy .map - and one list may mix them.

When this service owns its mappings, it collects the MappingResourceHolder beans (usually CustomMappings instances) of the application context itself, so no further beans are required: 

    <bean id="mappingService"
          class="org.openehealth.ipf.commons.spring.map.SpringBidiMappingService"/>
Collecting happens in afterSingletonsInstantiated(), i.e. from within finishBeanFactoryInitialization and thus before the ContextRefreshedEvent that starts e.g. the Camel context. Contributions can be ordered relative to each other with Spring's @Order / Ordered on the MappingResourceHolder bean.

Reading resources is left to a SpringMappings: one this service creates for itself, or, with SpringBidiMappingService(SpringMappings), the application's bean, which then does the collecting so that the mappings the two share are read exactly once.

Since:
3.1

      public SpringBidiMappingService(SpringMappings mappings)
      Deprecated, for removal: This API element is subject to removal in a future version.
      Adapts mappings somebody else owns, so that an application can keep using the untyped service while the mappings themselves are configured, and read, through SpringMappings. The SpringMappings must be a bean of the application context, since it collects the MappingResourceHolder beans itself; one created in place and handed in here never does.
      Parameters:
      mappings - the mappings to delegate to
